titleEn: A night-sky mystery: why do stars twinkle while planets do not?
summaryEn: Look up at the night sky and you will see some points of light flickering constantly and others holding still, shining steadily. The flickering points are usually stars; the steady ones are usually planets such as Venus, Mars or Jupiter. The light from both passes through the same atmosphere. The difference lies in their size on the sky: a star is almost a point, while a planet is a small disc, wide enough for the fluctuations caused by the atmosphere to cancel each other out.
